newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse trade at record high.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse trade at record high.

text.p: Germany's DAX index opened bourse trade at a record high on Thursday and stayed at higher levels early on, boosted by massive overnight Wall Street gains and the seemingly unshakeable resilience of the U.S. dollar.
The DAX, which gauges trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, stood at 3,224.18 points, up 8.04 points or 0.25 percent, having opened at 3,229.74 points and finding support from the futures market.
"If the futures market keeps up the advance, then we could see a rally like we did on Wednesday," said one trader.

Dealings during the bourse session could see the DAX climb to 3,250 points as the market found support from export sensitive shares posting gains, including carmakers such as Volkswagen AG, which was up 15 marks at 817.50 marks.
But some traders said the market was overbought and was due for a correction after the recent heady gains. Any breakdown on Wall Street would also heavily influence the DAX, they said.
Market attention focused on electronics group Siemens AG, which rose five pfennigs to 87.10 marks early on, having hit record highs in pre-bourse electronic trade.
Siemens said on Thursday it has revised upward its outlook for sales and incoming orders for both the 1996/97 business year and also the 1997/98 business year.

Among other shares, utility group Viag AG was down nine marks at 703.50 marks after the Berliner Zeitung newspaper reported on Thursday that the leaders of rival utility Veba AG and British Telecom were in secret talks about cooperation in the telecommunications industry.
Viag and BT currently have a partnership but Veba is seeking a new partner after Britain's Cable and Wireless pulled out of the alliance.
